source: A force is a push or a pull. Forces can start something moving, stop it, speed it up, slow it down or change its direction. Balanced forces cancel; unbalanced forces change motion.
Thinking a ball keeps rolling only while something pushes it. A rolling ball slows down because friction pushes back, not because its push "runs out".
Kick a ball, pull a wagon, open a door: each time you use a force.
A force is a push or a pull. A force can start something moving, stop it, make it faster or slower, or change its direction.

Forces have a size (strong or weak) and a direction. When two equal forces push opposite ways, as in a tug-of-war that nobody is winning, they are balanced and nothing changes. When one side is stronger, the forces are unbalanced and the rope moves toward it.
Some forces need touching; magnets and gravity work from a distance.
Two children push a box from opposite sides. One pushes hard, one pushes gently. What happens?
The box slides away from the child pushing hard.
The pushes are not equal, so the forces are unbalanced.
The box moves the way the harder push points.
Thinking a moving thing needs a push to keep going. A puck on smooth ice glides a long way. Things slow down because friction or air pushes against them.
Going further. Newton's Laws of Motion in the Science Lab, and Forces in Physical Science when you are older.
